title: Registration and Attach · 5G SA / LTE
description: Investigate Aurora's registration rejections after switching profiles between operators; compare 5G SA, the LTE control and the Boreal CDUT.

dut-vantis-zenith.label: Aurora · Vantis → Zenith · 5G SA
dut-vantis-zenith.title: Registration rejection cascade

evidence.title: Attempt 1 · previous operator context
evidence.html: On PCI 177, SIB1 advertises PLMN 724/085. The Registration Request uses SUCI 724/085 and receives 5GMM Cause #3 · Illegal UE.

evidence.title: Attempt 2 · target PLMN, old SUCI
evidence.html: On PCI 201, the selected PLMN is already 724/078, but the SUCI sent still carries Home-Network-Id 724/085. The network rejects with 5GMM Cause #11 · PLMN not allowed.

evidence.title: Attempt 3 · identity aligned
evidence.html: The new Registration Request presents SUCI 724/078; Authentication, Security Mode, Registration Accept and Registration Complete follow.

evidence.title: The failure happens after acquisition and RRC
evidence.html: PSS/SSS, MIB, SIB1 and RRC Setup complete in the rejected attempts. The divergence is in the NAS registration sequence, not in cell detection.

dut-vantis-zenith.notice: The attached log covers the 3 attempts of one of the five switches in scenario 1; the document does not say which. The log duration (4.55 s, from PSS/SSS detection to Registration Complete) matches the time of switch 03. There are no individual logs for the other switches. The exact internal causality of the SUCI transition is not proven by these logs: correlate the profile state and the provisioned identity.

dut-zenith-nimbus.label: Aurora · Zenith → Nimbus · 5G SA
dut-zenith-nimbus.title: The same cascade on another operator
dut-zenith-nimbus.state: NR SA · registered on the 3rd attempt

evidence.title: Anomaly repeated on another PLMN
evidence.html: All five Zenith → Nimbus switches also require three attempts in 5G SA.

evidence.title: Similar radio conditions
evidence.html: RSRP −83/−84 dBm and RSRQ −8 dB on the Zenith and Nimbus cells, respectively.

evidence.title: No individual modem log provided
evidence.html: The document reports the aggregate result, but the attached Aurora log covers only one switch of scenario 1.

evidence.title: Comparative evidence across scenarios
evidence.html: Recurrence across two operator transitions weakens the hypothesis of a single cell as an isolated cause.

dut-zenith-nimbus.notice: Times/ranges come from the challenge document. No individual log was provided for this transition; we do not infer specific NAS causes without the corresponding capture.
dut-zenith-nimbus.logLabel: No individual HTML log for scenario 2; see the case document and the aggregate results.

Registration completes after three attempts in each of the five switches.
Total times between 4.58 and 4.75 s. No individual call flow available.

cdut-boreal.label: Boreal · Vantis → Zenith · 5G SA
cdut-boreal.title: Boreal registers on the first attempt
cdut-boreal.description: Boreal · Vantis (724/085) → Zenith (724/078) · same cells as scenario 1

evidence.title: Same site and same cells
evidence.html: The CDUT accesses PCI 201/PLMN 724/078; the network accepts the Registration Request already carrying SUCI 724/078.

evidence.title: Complete NAS sequence
evidence.html: Authentication Request/Response, Security Mode Command/Complete, Registration Accept and Registration Complete.

evidence.title: 5G SA registration at first try
evidence.html: 5/5 switches complete on the first attempt; the detailed log shows a single successful attempt.

evidence.title: The contrast points to the DUT, it does not prove the implementation
evidence.html: DUT and CDUT differ in SIM/identity state and hardware; the control localizes the deviation in Aurora but does not by itself identify the internal mechanism.

cdut-boreal.notice: Boreal reference log: one attempt, 19 messages. Note: the log lasts 0.82 s (from PSS/SSS detection to Registration Complete), less than any total time for scenario 4 in the case (0.98–1.15 s); the document does not define when the measurement starts. The 5/5 switch report is aggregate; there are not five individual log files.
